summary:
I followed the planner's steps. Nothing was compiled or run. Early on I made one shell call by mistake; the harness refused it and nothing ran. After that I only read and edited files.

clipboard.rs (new, `mod clipboard;` after `mod cli;`): `Clipboard { write: Sink }` with `system()` and `copy()`. `system()` pipes the text into `pbcopy`. `piped` always waits for the program, then returns any feed error, then checks the exit status with `ensure!`. `test_support` has `Copied`, `recording()` and `broken()`. Tests: `cat` gives Ok, `false` gives Err, a missing program's error says it did not start.

conversation.rs: new field `prompts: Vec<usize>`, filled only by `say`. Private helpers `unfinished_from`, `finished_answer`, `prompt_before` and `text_at` (uses `get`, no indexing). Public `last_answer` and `last_exchange` ("{prompt}\n\n{answer}"). Six tests cover the planner's cases. Decision: `last_answer` must return `&str`, so it returns one Root entry. If a chain report arrives mid-stream, the answer is stored as two entries and only the part after the report is copied. This is rare.

tui/app.rs: `Services.clipboard`, private `App.clipboard`, `pub(super) status_note`. `handle` clears the note on its first line. Keys 'y' and 'Y' go to `copy_answer` and `copy_block` in `run_command`; the free fn `copy_note` builds the message. Six tests: exact table copy with its character count, Y copies "one\n\nfirst", the block before a still-printing answer is copied, an empty chat says nothing to copy, the next key clears the note, a broken clipboard reports "not copied: no clipboard here". Decision: key releases also clear the note; macOS sends none unless keyboard enhancement is on, and ratatui::init() leaves it off.

tui.rs: `COMMAND_HINT` lists both keys (88 characters, fits the 100-column test screen). `hint` returns the note if set, otherwise `mode_hint`, the old hint chain. Test: Ctrl-X y shows "answer copied · characters: 5", the next key brings back READING_HINT.

session.rs passes `Clipboard::system()`. README has a paragraph about copying blocks. No new dependencies, no comments, every match is exhaustive, imports in rustfmt order.
